sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Amit Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Sudhir Kumar Rai, learned counsel for the complainant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.
The FIR in question was lodged alleging that the daughter of the informant was enticed by the applicant and thereafter wrong was committed on her.

It was stated that the applicant fled away from the spot, subsequently in the statement under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she was in love with the applicant for the last two years and were on talking terms.
She also stated that she did not resist.

sentences.text: 1 3. Learned A.G.A. as well as the counsel for the complainant opposed the bail prayer.

4. Considering the two statements depicting that the victim and the applicant were in love each other for the last two years and the tentative age of the victim being around 16 years, the applicant who is in custody since 30.05.2024 and has no criminal history is enlarged on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Sudhir Yadav be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 103 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Asoha, District Unnao, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
